response.reason: The cited clause (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Art. 26(3)) establishes the requirement that if the country of origin or place of provenance of a food is given and it differs from that of its primary ingredient, the origin of the primary ingredient must also be given or indicated as different. The verdict turns on this requirement, stating that both origins are given and are the same, thus satisfying the obligation. The clause is directly relevant and supports the verdict.
